facts.raw_span: 10-year history of treatment with various medications
mild sinking of the right leg
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis: Clear fluid, normal glucose level, increased protein level, 108 cells/mL
T2 fluid-attenuated inversion recovery showed hyperintense lesion in the brainstem and cerebellum
Follow-up MRI Description: Reduced signal change on T2-weighted images, increased contrast enhancement showing ringlike appearance

families.label: Autoimmune
scope_in: history of treatment with immunomodulatory medications

families.label: Autoimmune
scope_in: history of treatment with immunomodulatory medications

concepts.why: The patient's history of treatment with immunomodulatory medications and impaired extraocular movement suggest an autoimmune disorder, and the presence of moderate tetraparesis and abnormal cerebrospinal fluid analysis support a diagnosis of Multiple Sclerosis

The patient's symptoms of fever, neck stiffness, and abnormal cerebrospinal fluid analysis, combined with the presence of a hyperintense lesion in the brainstem and cerebellum, suggest a diagnosis of Neurosyphilis

The patient's history of treatment with immunomodulatory medications and the presence of a hyperintense lesion in the brainstem and cerebellum, which showed increased contrast enhancement on follow-up MRI, suggest a diagnosis of Lymphoma
The patient's symptoms of fever, neck stiffness, and abnormal cerebrospinal fluid analysis, combined with the presence of a ringlike appearance on follow-up MRI, suggest a diagnosis of Brain Abscess

The patient's history of treatment with immunomodulatory medications and the presence of impaired extraocular movement and moderate tetraparesis suggest a diagnosis of Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy

The patient's symptoms of fever, neck stiffness, and abnormal cerebrospinal fluid analysis, combined with the presence of a hyperintense lesion in the brainstem and cerebellum, suggest a diagnosis of Subacute Sclerosing Panencephalitis
The patient's history of treatment with immunomodulatory medications and the presence of impaired extraocular movement and moderate tetraparesis suggest a diagnosis of CNS Vasculitis

The patient's symptoms of fever, neck stiffness, and abnormal cerebrospinal fluid analysis, combined with the presence of a hyperintense lesion in the brainstem and cerebellum, suggest a diagnosis of Toxoplasmosis

rationales.F01: Long history of treatment with various medications suggests a chronic condition like Multiple Sclerosis.
rationales.F02: No history of severe lymphocytopenia reduces the likelihood of Lymphoma and Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy.
rationales.F11: Hyperintense lesion in the brainstem and cerebellum is highly suggestive of Multiple Sclerosis or Brain Abscess.
rationales.F12: Ringlike appearance on follow-up MRI is highly suggestive of Brain Abscess.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms such as dizziness, nausea, moderate tetraparesis, fever, and neck stiffness, along with the cerebrospinal fluid analysis showing increased protein level and positive culture, and the MRI findings of a hyperintense lesion in the brainstem and cerebellum with contrast enhancement, are more consistent with a brain abscess than multiple sclerosis.

rationales.F12: Ringlike appearance on follow-up MRI is highly suggestive of Brain Abscess.
